note: Real A100 run, 2026-09-14 (Round6_NO_Peak_Stress_Fixed_Location_MultiRes.ipynb). Same fixed-location peak-PK1-stress metric as no_peak_stress_fixed_location_B1_neo_hookean.json (compute_peak_stress_error, same x_star/peak_ref since fine_N_for_peak/seed/material are identical), but for the NEW multi-res checkpoint (trained N=21,33,101,201; checkpoint fingerprint cb318c4694d820152d018bcb3a2caa6be4528f3654a59cc8aa2482e9cd495f86, verified before this run). Checkpoint identity verified by fingerprint before running. HEADLINE: peak-stress error improved at every single N (e.g. N=1401: 0.7359 -> 0.4142), and unlike the old checkpoint, is now BETTER than torch-fem's own best measured low-N peak-stress error (0.62 at N=49, see torchfem_full_qoi_low_N_result.json) for every NO resolution from N=29 upward -- meaning torch-fem cannot match the new checkpoint's peak-stress accuracy anywhere in the tested N=3-49 range for most resolutions (would need FEM N>49). This flips the previous 'coarsest suitable FEM' conclusion, which was previously bound by peak stress (matched at a moderate FEM N=17-45) precisely because the OLD checkpoint's peak-stress accuracy was so poor a coarse FEM's own slow-converging peak-stress error could still beat it somewhere in the tested range. Same near-domain-corner-singularity caveat as before still applies to this metric for BOTH methods (x_star is unchanged, still essentially the (0,0) corner) -- this should still be reported with that caveat, not as an unqualified win.
